Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories Email server not responding on smartphone or tablet (revised guide) ( Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories): # Troubleshooting Email Connection Issues on Your smartphone
If you're having trouble accessing your email on your smartphone, here are some steps you can take to resolve the issue.
## Step 1: Check Email Access on a PC
First, try accessing your email on a personal computer. This helps determine if the problem is with your phone's connection or your email account itself. If you can sign in and access your email on a PC, your phone might not be connected to Wi-Fi or mobile data.
## Step 2: Verify Your Phone's Internet Connection
Ensure your phone is connected to a stable Wi-Fi or mobile data network.
Swipe down from the top of your phone's screen to open the Quick settings panel.
Touch and hold the Wi-Fi icon to check your connection status.
Alternatively, go to Settings, tap Connections, and then tap Wi-Fi. To confirm your internet connection is working, try loading a webpage or performing a quick search.
## Step 3: Review Your Email Account Settings
Sometimes, changes made by your email provider on their server can cause connection problems. In such cases, you may need to remove and re-add your email account to your phone to apply the new configuration.
You can find instructions on how to remove your account and add it again at the provided links.
Before proceeding, make sure you have your email account's username and password readily available.
Remember that passwords are case-sensitive. Entering the password incorrectly will prevent your phone from connecting to your email server.
## Step 4: Clear the Email App's Cache and Data
Clearing the cache and data for your email app can resolve temporary glitches.
To clear the app's cache:
Navigate to Settings.
Tap Apps.
Select your email app.
Tap Storage.
Tap Clear cache.
To clear the app's data:
Navigate to Settings.
Tap Apps.
Select your email app.
Tap Storage.
Tap Clear data, and then tap OK.
Clearing the app's data will reset it to its original settings, effectively wiping it clean.
## Step 6: Contact Your Email Service Provider
If you have followed all the above steps and are still experiencing difficulties with your email connection, it is recommended to contact your email service provider directly for further assistance.

Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories Blank or black display on a smartphone or tablet (revised guide) ( Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories): ### Step 1: Check for Physical Damage and Liquid Exposure
First, please carefully inspect your phone or tablet, charger, and USB cable for any physical damage or signs of liquid exposure.
Please remove any cases or accessories that might be covering the charging port or buttons. Examine the USB connections for any corrosion or bent pins. The USB connection should feel secure with minimal movement. Next, let's check the Liquid Damage Indicator (LDI). The LDI should normally appear solid white, or white with pink or purple X's. Here's how to check the LDI:
Turn off your phone or tablet. Insert the ejector tool into the small hole next to the SIM/MicroSD tray to eject the tray. Shine a flashlight into the SIM/MicroSD slot.
If the device has been exposed to moisture, the LDI will appear solid pink, purple, or red. If this is the case, your device will require service. If the device has not been exposed to moisture, the LDI will be solid white or solid white with pink or purple Xs. Normal LDIs
An LDI exposed to liquid
### Step 2: Force a Restart
If there's no physical or liquid damage, let's try to force a restart on your device. There are two methods for this:
Press and hold both the Power button (or Side button) and the Volume down button simultaneously for at least 20 seconds.
If your device has a removable battery, please remove the battery for 60 seconds, and then reinsert it.
### Step 3: Charge the Device
Now, please connect your phone or tablet to its appropriate charger and let it charge for at least 1 hour. It's important to note that the battery charging indicator might take up to 10 minutes to appear on the display.
### Step 4: Attempt to Power On
After charging, please disconnect the phone or tablet from the charger. Then, try to turn it on by pressing and holding the Power button (or Side button) for 15 to 20 seconds. You should see the TechCorp Nexa logo appear if it powers on successfully.
If the screen turns on, it indicates that your device needed a charge. Please turn off your device and reconnect it to the appropriate charger until it is fully charged. If the screen still fails to turn on after completing all these steps, your device may require service. In this case, please contact the Customer Support Center for further assistance.

siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories Use Multi window and App pairs on your smartphone or tablet (revised guide) ( Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories): Note: If this is your first time using enhanced edge features, you will need to complete the tutorial. Available screens and settings may vary by wireless service provider, software version, and device model. Split screen view and pop-up view are not supported on the front screen of the Nexa Foldable series or Foldable series. Some apps do not support split screen view.
## Customize the Quick Access panel
Your device's Quick Access panel lets you quickly access frequently used apps and content. You can customize the panel, download new panels, and remove apps from the panel if needed. To find the panel, swipe left on the gray Quick Access panel handle, which is located on the right side of your screen. You can use the Settings, All apps, and Edit icons at the bottom of the panel to adjust your desired options.
## Use Multi window
You can use Multi window on your Nexa foldable and non-foldable devices. If you have a few favorite apps, you can even create app pairs!
From the screen's right side, swipe left to open the Quick Access panel. Tap the All apps icon (the grid). From here, you'll be able to see all of your current apps.To open an app in split screen view on Foldable devices, drag and drop it to the left, right, top, or bottom of the screen and then do the same for additional apps if desired. To open an app in pop-up view, just drag the app to the center. To open an app in split screen view on the Foldable front screen, or Foldable devices and non-foldable devices, drag and drop it to the top or bottom of the screen, and then do the same for another app. To open one in pop-up view, just drag the app to the center. You can also tap Recents, tap an app's icon, and then tap either Open in split screen view or Open in pop-up view.When you are in pop-up view, you can rearrange your opened apps by moving the windows to your liking. If you need a larger view for a certain app, tap the expand icon at the top to expand the window. When you are in split screen view, you can use the dividers between the apps to adjust the size of the windows. To create an app pair from split screen view, tap the dotted divider between the apps, and then tap the Add to app pair icon (the star). Then, select your desired location for the app pair. To close an app in split screen view or pop-up view, tap the blue divider at the top of the app's screen, and then tap the X icon. On foldable devices, your apps will remain active if you switch to Flex mode. Keep the phone propped open on a desk or in your hand to continue using split screen or pop-up view. Note: Flex mode is not supported on the Nexa TriFold X1. Multi window can also be used with the Stylus Pen on your One UI 5 Foldable! For instance, you can cross-reference documents and emails in Microsoft Office apps, such as Outlook and PowerPoint, and then make notes and suggestions using your Stylus Pen. On the Foldable and Tab series, you'll also be able to drag an app from the taskbar to open it in Multi window.
## Swipe gestures for Multi window
devices running One UI 6 or later have introduced a new feature that simplifies multitasking by allowing you to quickly move an open app into split screen or pop-up views using intuitive swipes. This streamlines your daily multitasking, making it easier to manage multiple apps simultaneously.
Navigate to and open Settings, and then tap Advanced features. Tap Multi window, and then tap the switches next to Swipe for split screen or Swipe for pop-up view.Once you've turned on these features, a two finger swipe from the bottom of the screen will move the current app into split screen mode. You can also use one finger to swipe in from either top corner to put the current app into a pop-up. You can drag the pop-up to the side of the screen to hide it, and then tap it again to bring it back to the center of the screen. Tap the top of the pop-up window to use additional options. Please see the "Use pop-up view" section for details. There are multiple ways to use Multi window:
Drag and drop apps from the Taskbar Drag and drop apps from the Quick Access panel Select apps from the Recents menu Drag and drop a URL or hyperlink Drag and drop apps from your notifications Use two-finger swipe gestures from the bottom or sides of the screen
## Exit Multi window
When you want to give Multi window a break and just use one app, you can close the split screen view.
To do this, tap the Home icon. This will close them completely on the Home screen but leave them together in Recents.
## Create an App pair
Note
The Quick Access panel is only available on certain device models.
Instead of separately opening apps you always use together, just create an App pair. That way, those two apps will open simultaneously in split screen view. If you're using the Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1 Ultra, or TriFold X1, you can create an App pair with three apps.
Swipe left to open the Quick Access panel. Touch and hold your desired app, and drag and drop it into the top portion of the screen.
Open the Quick Access panel again, and then drag and drop a second app into the bottom portion of the screen.
Tap the dotted divider between the two windows to change the orientation and create an App pair:
Tap the two arrows to swap the apps' positions. Tap the Add to app pair icon (it may have a plus sign or a star) to create an App pair. The App pair will be saved, although you may be prompted to select where you'd like to save the App pair to.
If you'd like to add a third app to the App pair, open Application Edge again, and then drag and drop the new app into your preferred position.
Note: Adding three apps to an App pair is only available on the Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, Foldable X1, TriFold X1, and Foldable X1 Ultra.
Once all the apps are on the screen, tap the dotted divider in the center, and then tap the Add to app pair icon. The three apps will be saved in a group.
## Useful App pairing ideas
Note
The Quick Access panel is only available on certain device models.
Can't think of any useful app pairing combinations? Here are some combinations to get those creative juices flowing.
Internet + Quick Notes: Browse the internet and take notes at the same time. Play Music + Maps: Play your jam while going on an adventure. Email + Phone: Never miss an email because of a long phone call. Camera + Gallery: Capture and manage your photos all at once. Contacts + Message: Network with your friends and create new connections. Quick Notes + Drive: Make a note and save it to your Google Drive.
## Remove shortcuts from Application Edge
Note
The Quick Access panel is only available on certain device models.
Maybe doing homework while playing a game isn't the best idea. Remove that shortcut to make room for a new one.

You can always add the shortcut back later, or add new Quick Access panels with additional apps that you'd like to use.
Glossary
Quick Access panel: A sliding panel on the side of the screen that provides quick access to apps, tools, and content.
Multi window: A feature that allows multiple applications to be displayed and used simultaneously on the screen in split screen or pop-up view.
Split screen view: A layout mode that divides the screen to run two or more apps side by side or stacked vertically.
Pop-up view: A multitasking mode where an app runs in a movable, resizable floating window over other apps.
App pair: A shortcut combination of two or three apps that open together in multi window mode with a single tap.
Flex mode: A specialized display mode for foldable devices that splits app interfaces when the phone is partially folded.
Stylus Pen: A stylus accessory designed for compatible devices to write, draw, and navigate with precision.

siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories Screen mirroring to your TechCorp TV (revised guide) ( Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories): # Screen Mirroring and Casting Explained
Hello! I can help you understand the difference between screen mirroring and casting, and how to use these features with your devices.
## Screen Mirroring vs. Casting
As technology advances, so does the vocabulary associated with it. Terms like "screen mirroring" or "casting" can be confusing. Both allow you to stream videos, photos, and other content from your phone to your Smart TV. Here's a more in-depth look:
### What is Screen Mirroring?
Screen mirroring lets you mirror your phone's screen to a bigger screen, like a Smart TV. Exactly what's showing on your phone will appear on the TV, whether it's an app, a photo, or a video. Any action you take on your phone, like navigating to a different app, will also be shown on the TV screen.
On devices, this feature is called Smart View. You can easily mirror your screen with Smart View by tapping the Smart View icon and following a few simple steps.
For iPhones, the screen mirroring feature is called AirPlay, and it functions similarly by mirroring images, videos, or other media. Using AirPlay is similar to, but slightly different from, using Smart View. No matter which device you have, screen mirroring is a great way to share content from your phone directly on your Smart TV.Nexa Smart View interfaceApple AirPlay interface
### What is Casting?
Casting is similar to screen mirroring in that you use your mobile device to control what's on your TV. However, instead of showing the same content on both devices, your mobile device acts like a remote control.
Certain apps, like Netflix or YouTube, allow you to cast videos from your phone directly to a big screen. Even if you don't have a Smart TV, you can use third-party casting devices like Chromecast or an Amazon Fire Stick to stream videos.
To screen cast to your TechCorp TV, ensure both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network. Then, use either the built-in Smart View feature or the SmartThings app.
For Smart View: Swipe down from your mobile device's top screen and tap Smart View. Select your TV and confirm the connection request on the TV screen.
For SmartThings: Add your TV to the app and choose Smart View. Confirm the connection request on the TV.Screen mirroring interface on a smartphone
When you're casting, the video or movie will only appear on the TV. You can control the video on your phone, and you can also close the app and do other things without interrupting the video, as long as the phone remains connected. It's a convenient way to enjoy both a movie and your phone.
If you have an iPhone or iPad, you can cast to your TV using AirPlay.
## Mirror Your TV with Smart View
You can project photos or videos from your phone or tablet onto your TV. You can also do the opposite and stream your TV to your phone or tablet's screen!
Important notes:
Make sure your TV is turned on and connected to the same Wi-Fi network as your phone.
Some TVs may require you to switch inputs or turn on screen mirroring.
Compatibility with non-TechCorp TVs may vary or may not be available. Check your TV's user manual for specific details.
Smart View is not an app you download on your phone; it's located in the Quick settings panel.
Open the Quick settings panel by swiping down from the top right of your screen. Tap Smart View.
Select your TV from the list of Available devices, and then tap Start now. If prompted, enter a PIN or allow access to complete the connection.
Your device's screen will now appear on the TV.
If you want to stream the TV's screen to your phone or tablet (if your TV supports it), navigate back to the Smart View main page, tap Other device → Phone, and then select your TV.
To switch back, tap Phone → Other device. When you are done using Smart View, tap the Smart View icon on your phone, and then tap Disconnect. If you need help editing the icons in the Quick settings panel, check out our guide.
## Project Your Windows 10 or Windows 11 PC to a TV
### Requirements
Before you can enjoy the show, make sure your PC and TV meet the correct requirements.
Most PCs that run Windows 10 or Windows 11 will support this feature. To check if your PC is compatible, press the Windows key + P key on your keyboard. A Project action bar will open. To be compatible, this action bar must contain the link "Connect to a wireless display." If it is not there, your device is not compatible.
Most TechCorp Smart TVs will support screen mirroring and casting.
Make sure that both the TV and PC are operating on the same Wi-Fi network.
### Mirror Your Screen
On your PC, select Start, then begin typing Bluetooth and other device settings and select it when it appears.
Select Add device or Add Bluetooth or other device. Then, select Wireless display or dock.
Select your TV once its name is displayed. If prompted, select Allow on your TV.
Now your PC's screen will be mirrored to the TV.
### Disconnect the Devices
Once you are finished mirroring your screen, it's time to disconnect.
On your PC, select Start, then begin typing Bluetooth and other device settings and select it when it appears.
If you're using Windows 10, simply select the connected device. If you're using Windows 11, select More options (the three vertical dots) next to the device you want to disconnect.
Select Remove device, and then select Yes.
To view the latest compatible Nexa Books, check out our website.
## Access Smart View with SmartThings
You can mirror your device's display to a TV using the SmartThings app as well. First, make sure the TV is turned on and connected to your SmartThings account.
Using your phone or tablet, open the SmartThings app, and select the TV you would like to mirror to.
In the TV's settings page, tap More options (the three vertical dots), and then tap Mirror screen (Smart View).
Tap Start now. Give your TV permission to access your device, if needed. Note: This feature may not be available on the PC version of SmartThings.
## Tips for Mirroring with Smart View
Here are some tips if you're having trouble mirroring your phone or tablet:
If your phone or tablet will not display, it may need permission from the TV. Restart your device and TV, and then try connecting again. Make sure to select Allow when it displays on the TV. You should also try looking for software updates on your devices. If the problem persists, perform a factory data reset on the phone or tablet.
On a TechCorp TV, you can bypass allowing permission for your device to access your TV. From All Settings on your TV, navigate to All Settings, then Connections, and then External Device Manager. Navigate to Device Connect Manager, and then select Access Notification. Set this to Off to automatically connect with the device when using Smart View. From the Device Connect Manager screen, you can also select Device List to manage the devices connected to your TV.
If your screen keeps turning off, change the screen timeout settings. From Settings, search for and select Screen timeout. From there, adjust the settings so your phone or tablet stays on for longer.
If the Smart View menu is minimized, tap the Smart View icon on your phone or tablet. The Smart View Control menu is only displayed on your connected device.
If the device's image looks small on your screen, you can make it a little bigger by changing the aspect ratio. On your phone or tablet, tap the Smart View icon, and then tap More options (the three vertical dots). Tap Settings, and then tap Phone aspect ratio. From there you can choose your desired aspect ratio. Most TVs will look best with a 16:9 aspect ratio.
If you are using a VPN, please disconnect from it if a VPN setting error occurs.
If you are still having difficulty, check out our screen mirroring troubleshooting guide.

siis_response.title: Touchscreen issues on a smartphone or tablet (revised guide)
siis_response.content:
Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories Touchscreen issues on a smartphone or tablet (revised guide) ( Smartphone,Tablet,Others Mobile,Mobile Accessories): # Troubleshooting Touchscreen Issues
I understand you're experiencing some issues with your device's touchscreen. Let's go through some steps to help resolve this.
## 2. Restarting Your Device
A simple restart can often resolve minor issues. The process for restarting varies by model:
For devices with a Power button: Press and hold the Power button, then tap Restart. Tap Restart again to confirm.
For devices with a Side button: Swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers to open the Quick settings panel. Tap the Power icon, then tap Restart. Tap Restart again to confirm.
If the touchscreen is completely unresponsive, you can force a restart by pressing and holding the Volume down button and the Power button (or Side button) simultaneously for about 10 seconds. Once the device turns off, press the Power button or Side button again to turn it back on.
## 3. Charger Issues
A damaged charger might not be supplying enough power to your device, which could lead to touchscreen malfunctions. If you suspect this is the case, please try using a different, undamaged charger. It's also a good practice to avoid using the touchscreen while your device is charging.
## 4. Full Screen Gesture Function
If you're using the full screen gesture function, your touch inputs might be misinterpreted as gestures, preventing them from being recognized. To prevent this, you can disable the full screen gesture function. Go to Settings, tap Display, and then tap Navigation bar. Select Buttons to turn off full screen gestures.
## 5. Touch Sensitivity Setting
If the Touch sensitivity setting is enabled when you are not using a protective film, the touchscreen might become overly sensitive and malfunction. To turn off this feature, navigate to Settings, tap Display, and then tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity to disable it.
## 6. Software Updates
Keeping your device's software up to date is important for smooth performance. You should also check for updates for any third-party apps you use, as these can sometimes affect gesture customization.
## 7. Safe Mode
Safe mode can help us identify if a recently installed third-party app is causing the problem. To enter Safe mode:
Press and hold the Power button (or Side button) and the Volume down button at the same time.
Alternatively, swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers and tap the Power icon.
Touch and hold Power off, then tap Safe mode. Once in Safe mode, you can try removing any third-party apps that were recently updated or installed around the time the issue began. To exit Safe mode, simply restart your phone or tablet, and it will boot up normally.
## 8. Factory Data Reset
A factory data reset should only be considered as a last resort, after trying all the previous steps. Please be aware that this action will erase all data and content from your device. Before proceeding, it is crucial to back up your personal data to avoid losing it.
To perform a factory data reset:
Navigate to and open Settings.
Tap General management.
Tap Reset.
Tap Factory data reset.
Swipe to and tap Reset.
Tap Delete all. You will need to enter your TechCorp account credentials to complete the reset. Your device will then reset, and you will need to go through the initial setup process.
## 9. Further Assistance
If the issue persists after trying all these steps, please reach out to Customer Support for further assistance.
